# Computing time {#sec-app-time}

Times are wall-clock seconds on one core. They come from four sources: (A) a benchmark on one
local core with Gaussian data, $G = 100$ curves, $D = 61$ grid points and the default bases
(`r max(time_tab$n[time_tab$data == "A"])` replicates over the dependent error processes of the
simulation); (B) the comparator runs on a computing cluster, Gaussian main-factorial settings and
plasmode datasets with independent source curves, $G = 40$ to 138; (C) the smoothing-parameter-term runs on
the main-factorial settings at the default signal ($G = 40$ and 100); (D) the same terms on the
plasmode data. @fig-time shows the median, the quartiles, the 90% quantile and the maximum per method; Supplement S7 lists them.

```{r}
#| label: fig-time
#| fig-cap: "Computing time in seconds per fit or per covariance, by method and data source (A: local benchmark, Gaussian, G = 100, D = 61; B: comparator runs, Gaussian synthetic settings and plasmode datasets with independent source curves; C: main-factorial settings; D: plasmode data); n: number of timed fits or covariances; log scale. Point: median; thick bar: quartiles; thin bar: up to the 90% quantile; cross: maximum. CL2 and the smoothing-parameter terms are computed on top of an existing fit. Times for pcre and GLS include the REML pilot fit and, where used, the FPCA of its residual curves."
#| fig-height: 3.6
fig_time(time_tab)
```

A curve-blocked NCV fit costs about `r f(tt("curve-blocked NCV fit", "A") / tt("REML fit", "A"), 1)`
times a REML fit; the profiled AR(1) model about `r f(tt("AR(1) working model (profiled)", "A") / tt("REML fit", "A"), 0)`
times, because it refits the model at each value of $\rho$. The CL2 covariance of a REML fit adds a
median `r f(tt("CL2 covariance (REML fit)", "A"), 2)` s, its Satterthwaite degrees of freedom add a
median `r f(satt_df_time, 1)` s per replicate for all four estimands in the main factorial,
`r f(SATXI$df_time_median, 1)` s in the other synthetic settings and `r f(SATPI$df_time_median, 1)` s on the
plasmode data (cluster nodes).

Times for GLS and pcre include the REML pilot fit and the FPCA of its residual curves (the raw GLS covariance needs no FPCA). GLS then takes a median of `r f(tt("GLS, FPCA residual covariance", "B"), 1)` s; pcre's time
grows quickly with the number of curves and grid points (median `r f(tt("pcre fit", "B"), 0)` s,
90% quantile `r f(tt("pcre fit", "B", "q90"), 0)` s, maximum `r f(tt("pcre fit", "B", "max"), 0)` s).
CL2 on these fits adds a median of `r f(tt("CL2 on a GLS fit", "B"), 2)` s (GLS) and
`r f(tt("CL2 on a pcre fit", "B"), 1)` s (pcre). The curve bootstrap with 199 refits takes a median
of `r f(tt("curve bootstrap (199 refits)", "B"), 0)` s and up to
`r f(tt("curve bootstrap (199 refits)", "B", "max"), 0)` s per dataset. The smoothing-parameter
uncertainty terms (curve scores, Hessian and infinitesimal jackknife) add a median of
`r f(tt("smoothing-parameter term, REML", "C"), 1)` s to a REML fit and
`r f(tt("smoothing-parameter term, NCV", "C"), 1)` s to a Gaussian NCV fit. The one-step bias
correction of the NCV estimate needs one linear solve with $p \times p$ matrices and was not timed
separately.
